source_correspondence: O0 fixes the rapid-position plus Fourier-multiplier symbol class, its unique spatial-infinity decomposition, Schwartz action and all-real Peetre bounds.
O1 derives the exact ordered Fourier product by absolute integration and proves every mixed derivative and rapid-position estimate with an inner/outer frequency split.
O2 supplies the full Taylor integral remainder, adjoint sign and every one-third-gain seminorm; smoothing symbols form a two-sided ideal.
O3 proves all-real Sobolev continuity by weighted Fourier Schur estimates, plus density, transpose extension, compact-distribution finite order and smoothing.
O4 constructs supported asymptotic sums with explicit radii and proves both ordered matrix parametrix identities modulo smoothing, preserving possible low-frequency kernels.
O5 extends the actual zero-free Airy multiplier without changing the smaller cone. Positive real part gives the global lower bound; cutoff derivatives obey all relative one-third estimates.

O6 factors the variable complex-matrix boundary operator exactly, sums the ordered correction, proves both inverse identities including smoothing remainders, and derives hypoelliptic regularity without assuming it.
O7 proves the exact ordered reflection cancellation and zero-order Sobolev bounds; matching and converse identities retain the precise smoothing errors.

O8 proves local elliptic extension and separated-support localization. Graph conjugation uses earlier all-real Sobolev maps under an explicit actual-representation hypothesis; invariance of exotic symbols is not assumed.

X1 proves a Gaussian coefficient gives different pointwise and operator inverses. X2 computes the exact transition derivative excluding ordinary symbol order. X3 proves the finite-residual sign and each two-thirds improvement.
Seven finite groups include 57 exact checks and 41 separately labelled numerical samples. The original three-panel illustration states its exact normalizations and proof locators.

The phase, coupled matrix amplitudes, full differential-equation representation and weak energy-domain transfer remain required for general strict propagation. No general propagation theorem is certified by this operator step.
